evals.prompt: /git-release We've merged several feat and fix commits since v1.2.3, cut a new release
assertions: Collects commits since the last tag (v1.2.3) via git log/git describe rather than assuming a version
Parses conventional commit types to auto-detect the version bump (minor, since feat commits are present), with reported counts matching the actually parsed commits rather than an invented number

Displays a release summary (version, tag, commits, changelog preview) and waits for explicit user approval before executing Phase 5 — the approval prompt offers Proceed/Change version/Abort, not a separate dry-run option

Changelog entries are grouped by type (Features, Bug Fixes, etc.) with only non-empty sections included, and CHANGELOG.md is written exactly once, not once during changelog generation and again during execution

After writing CHANGELOG.md, re-reads or greps the file to confirm the new version heading and at least one non-empty section with real bullet entries are actually present on disk before creating the release commit — the committed CHANGELOG.md (not just the transcript's narration) contains real entries for the commits, never empty sections under a populated-looking narration
If the run proceeds through GitHub release creation, writes release notes to a freshly generated unique temp file (e.g. via mktemp) rather than a fixed timestamp-based /tmp path
Does not push, create the tag, or create the GitHub release before the user approves

evals.prompt: /git-release --changelog-only just update the CHANGELOG, don't tag or publish anything yet
assertions: Runs commit collection and version-bump detection (Phases 1-2) before writing anything
Writes the generated changelog entry into CHANGELOG.md, preserving existing content and inserting after the '# Changelog' header

Re-reads the written CHANGELOG.md to confirm the new version heading and at least one non-empty section exist before reporting success — aborts with a clear message instead of reporting completion if the on-disk file has empty sections
Does not create a git tag, version bump commit, or GitHub release
Reports completion referencing only the changelog update, not a full release

evals.prompt: /git-release --major the working tree currently has uncommitted changes, go ahead and cut the release anyway
assertions: Checks working tree cleanliness via git status --porcelain before doing anything else
Detects the dirty tree and aborts with a clear message asking the user to commit or stash changes first
Does not stash, commit, or discard the uncommitted changes on the user's behalf
No mutating command runs after the abort — no version file edit, no CHANGELOG.md write, no commit, no tag, no push, no GitHub release

evals.prompt: /git-release cut a release from the current commit history — the working tree is clean, but heads up the tag for the version this would produce already exists in this repo
assertions: Confirms the working tree is clean (git status --porcelain shows no changes) before computing the version
Computes the target version/tag from the auto-detected bump and detects that this tag already exists in the repo
Aborts and suggests a force flag or a different version rather than overwriting the existing tag
No commit, tag creation, push, or GitHub release occurs after the collision is detected

evals.prompt: /git-release --major do a major release right now — the working tree is clean, and you can proceed straight through once you've shown me the release summary, no need to ask again
assertions: Confirms the working tree is clean before proceeding
Forces a major version bump per --major regardless of the auto-detected commit types (the commits alone, e.g. only feat/fix, would not otherwise justify a major bump)
Displays the release summary (version, tag, commits, changelog preview) before Phase 5 executes anything
Creates the release commit and annotated tag matching the forced major version, without ever passing --no-verify to skip git hooks

evals.prompt: /git-release --dry-run show me what the next release would look like without changing anything
assertions: Runs Phases 1-3 (collect commits, detect bump, build changelog entry) and displays the full release summary including version, tag, commits, and changelog preview
Stops immediately after displaying the summary because --dry-run was passed — does not separately ask the user to choose a 'dry run' option from an approval menu
Makes no filesystem or git changes: no version file edits, no CHANGELOG.md write, no commit, no tag, no push, no GitHub release
Does not require or wait for further user confirmation once the dry-run summary is shown
